confidence: Each task had one scored submission. The first attempt at the hardest Voiceover Editing task hit a quota limit and was excluded. The attempt after re-dispatch counted. The quota issue was treated as an environment incident. Most roles have only three tasks. Taste and B-roll Editing each have two scored tasks. Review and Shot Finding were consistent on this set, with limited evidence on how well that carries over to other footage. The original-audio subtitle errors came from a single task. Check the transcript source on similar tasks. Conclusions about its overall subtitle performance need more evidence.

avoid: Keep aesthetic decisions with an editor when there is no rules file.
Have an editor handle subtitles for original audio or tasks where the source of the reference transcript is unclear.
Review footage logs after delivery and verify the entries marked unsure.
Have an editor review its B-roll selections. It failed both tasks.
give: Use it for Review, especially to catch a few stray frames, repeated footage, and subtitle typos.
Use it to find shots in long videos and verify whether a specific shot appears.
Use it for a first pass on a voiceover edit. Check whether it trimmed the beginning or end of the main spoken content.
Use it to make revisions from clear notes.

honesty: No false claims were found. Evidence supported 110 of its reported claims, contradicted 0, and left 34 unverifiable. No actions were classified as out-of-directory access, internet access, or re-dispatch. On almost every task, it listed uncertainties for confirmation. It marked film titles it could not identify as unsure and explained why. On the third Voiceover Editing task, it reported writing a script and audio files to the session temporary directory and deleting them afterward. This was not classified as out-of-directory access. Several contact sheets had inconsistent source labels, so the grader could not verify their origin. They were excluded from the false claim count.
one_line: It scored 84.82 without speed and 84.78 with speed overall, passing 15 of the 22 scored tasks. It got all the answers right on the three Review tasks and was consistent at Shot Finding. Speed penalties were small. B-roll Editing and subtitles for original audio remained clear weaknesses.

roles.text: Its role score was 92.99 without speed, and it passed only one of three tasks. On the short clip logging task (SORT2), it identified corner watermarks, audio features, and duplicate assets. It marked 7 fields as unsure. Those fields covered watermarks, usability, and intended use. Its content quality score was 0.896, just below the 0.90 pass threshold. On the task to log film clips and ranges of repeated footage (SORT3), its content quality score was 0.893, also just below the 0.90 pass threshold. It lost points for a film title error and two incorrect dialogue judgments.

Its role score was 96.83 without speed, and it passed all three tasks. The hardest task (FIND3) asked it to check whether a specified shot appeared in a four-minute video. It reviewed the entire video, accurately reported its findings on the shots and timing cue. It earned full marks in 75.1 seconds. On the film identification task, it marked two entries as unsure and abstained from guessing.

Its role score was 98.18 without speed. It earned full marks on the first two tasks, which involved editing spoken recordings. On the task with two recordings (VO3), it checked the audio against the transcript and made mostly correct choices about what to keep. Its content quality score was 0.945, above the pass threshold. It trimmed parts of the opening and ending and clipped the end of one syllable. It failed both the check for preserving the main spoken content and the trap-handling check. The incomplete keep ranges also affected the latter. Under the new rules, it scored 94.54 without speed and still passed. The completeness of the main spoken content still needs review. The score uses the second attempt. The first run stopped after 83 seconds when it hit a quota limit, which was recorded separately as an environment incident.

Its role score was 28.29 without speed. On the first task, 2 of the 5 choices matched the usable final cut. On the longer explainer task, it matched 2 of the 7 scored items. It met the mandatory requirements on both tasks and failed both. Have an editor sign off on the final B-roll choices.

On the open-book task with editing rules available (TASTE1), all 20 choices matched the usable final cut. On the closed-book task without rules (TASTE2), 10 of 15 matched, for a content quality score of 0.333, below the pass threshold. Its choices diverged substantially from the usable final cut without a rules file. That finding is based on one task. The task that asks the model to watch footage and choose clip in and out points is for reference only and does not count toward the score.

Its role score was 100 without speed and 99.95 with speed, putting it among the top models in this role. It passed all three tasks. The hardest task (QC3) asked it to catch a few stray frames from adjacent shots, repeated footage, and subtitle typos. It got all the issues right and supplied the relevant timestamps. It took 160.1 seconds to check for black frames, white flashes, and watermarks on QC1. The new speed baseline barely reduced the score, which was 99.93 with speed.

Its role score was 91.67 without speed. It earned full marks on the two tasks with clear revision notes, taking 51.6 and 32.3 seconds respectively and leaving everything else untouched. On FIX3, it got part of the task right but missed part of the revision's scope. That fell short of the task requirements.

Its role score was 79.03 without speed. It passed the first two tasks and corrected the proper names to match the script. It made serious errors on the original-audio subtitle task (SUB3). It got the subtitle text wrong and shifted all the subtitles by 25.65 seconds. Text accuracy, timing alignment, and identification of the transcript source all scored poorly. The task scored 37.39 without speed and 37.31 with speed.

working_style: Median time from start to submission was 87.5 seconds per task, quick for this group of models. It completed 90% of tasks within 293.3 seconds. There were no timeouts, errors, or restarts on record. The median task involved 8.5 tool calls and 14.9 seconds of final self-checking. It routinely checked its work before delivery. Token usage does not affect the score. Across the 22 scored tasks, it produced 225,485 output tokens, including 113,737 reasoning tokens. Output and reasoning usage were both high. It sampled many frames on visual tasks, viewing images 35 times on the short clip logging task (SORT2). It answered every speed-test item with a known answer correctly. Reading one frame took 8.5 seconds, and the minimal task that asked for a one-sentence reply took 4.3 seconds from dispatch to submission. Both were quick. The long-form writing task took 58.7 seconds. Long output was slower relative to its short-task performance. Cost data was unavailable.
